motion.name: Entrance / Homepage
motion.trigger: First visit, after fonts and navigation are ready; animation-frame downloads do not gate the content.
motion.motion: Header links fade in and rise 12 px with a 140 ms delay and 70 ms step (power2.out). The portrait fades in, rises 18 px and scales .97 → 1; copy rises 18 px with a 200 ms step (power3.out). Portrait starts at 100 ms and copy at 300 ms in the content timeline.
motion.playback: Runs once per page load. Both desktop and mobile reveal the static poster and copy independently of the portrait turn buffer. The boot module starts the existing welcome turn only after both the portrait entrance and prepared welcome frames are ready. A failed or delayed frame download leaves the early content readable. Leaving the tab settles the entrance.
motion.reduced: Show the final content immediately. Missing GSAP or failed portrait preparation keeps the page readable.
motion.preview: The component preview is static. Open the live homepage to see its page entrance.

motion.name: Entrance / Reading content
motion.trigger: First paint, then each prepared block as it enters the viewport.
motion.motion: Fade 0 → 1 and rise 8px using cubic-bezier(.37,0,.63,1). The title leads the intro paragraphs. On About, the whole recommendations block follows the intro and the footer photo gallery follows the prose. Individual translate keeps the gallery’s horizontal centering and photo movement independent. Blocks enter in reading order with one shared step; newly visible batches continue the sequence behind visible first-paint blocks. Blocks passed above the viewport finish immediately and release their queue slots. Shorten waiting delays after that cleanup without restarting active fades; blocks still below the viewport retain their entrance.
motion.playback: Reading-page blocks appear once. Reverse scrolling, quote changes and photo panning do not replay them. The added media entrances are scoped to the About composition; standalone components and the photo experiment keep their existing behavior. Hash navigation, keyboard focus and history restoration expose the relevant content immediately. The 404 page reuses the CSS entrance for its title, copy and Back to home button at first paint, in that order.
motion.reduced: All reading content is visible without entrance animation. CSS first paint and the optional observer preserve readable content if JavaScript is unavailable.

motion.name: Portrait / Turn & interaction
motion.trigger: Prepared welcome frames, pointer movement, drag or keyboard input.
motion.motion: One welcome turn eases to the front with sine ease-in-out. Desktop pointer following reaches ±49° and softens within 1.5 portrait widths of the face. Drag allows full turns; release returns to the nearest front with a damped spring and a small overshoot. Android uses its separate touch player.
motion.playback: There is no idle loop. Manual input cancels the welcome and takes priority over follow/scroll. A new press interrupts the spring. Mobile scroll pose follows actual occlusion; menu close returns to the front. These interactions run on the live homepage; the portrait specimen shows static poses.
motion.reduced: Static front portrait; no animation-frame ZIP requests. Hidden tabs suspend movement; errors retain the poster.

motion.name: Entrance / Project content
motion.trigger: A card enters view and its own preview has loaded or failed.
motion.motion: Text fades in and rises 14 px with a 70 ms step (power2.out). Desktop artwork rises 14 px and fades over 800 ms. Mobile artwork uses a pure 1150 ms sine.inOut fade after 12% of the image is visible, capped at 48 px; visible description starts no earlier than 420 ms after the image, then actions 140 ms after description.
motion.playback: Decode and actual visibility gate the preview. A fast jump restores an image already passed so copy can continue. Returning all the way to the intro resets HOME reveals; ordinary card-to-card reverse scrolling keeps revealed content.
motion.reduced: Readable cards in normal flow; no reveal or overlapping scene animation. Image errors expose the existing Preview unavailable state.
motion.preview: The component preview shows the artwork and content. The live homepage runs the scroll-triggered entrance.

motion.name: Navigation / Mobile menu
motion.trigger: Activate the mobile menu toggle or close the menu.
motion.motion: The same two SVG strokes morph into a cross over 200 ms ease-in-out. Opening fades the panel over 280 ms (power2.out); links fade/rise 12 px over 320 ms with a 55 ms step, starting at 70 ms (power3.out). Closing sends links down 12 px over 240 ms in reverse order (power3.in), then fades the panel over 280 ms (power2.inOut).
motion.playback: Rapid toggles cancel the active timeline and follow the latest requested state. Scroll is locked while open; closing restores the page and relevant focus.
motion.reduced: Toggle and menu settle immediately. Missing GSAP retains working open/close controls; hidden/changed-layout transitions settle.

motion.name: Buttons / Directional arrows
motion.trigger: Hover with a fine pointer on desktop; primary touch contact on mobile.
motion.motion: Only the icon moves 4px in the arrow direction. Desktop hover holds the offset and pointer leave smoothly restores it. Touch plays one out-and-back movement, with the peak at45%. Labels, button bounds and arrow orientation stay fixed.
motion.playback: Repeated touch restarts the icon feedback. Native link navigation is immediate and may leave the page before the feedback completes. No synthetic clicks or navigation delay. Disabled controls stay static; hidden document and motion preference changes cancel touch feedback.
motion.reduced: Arrows stay static with reduced motion, including the DS reduced-motion specimen.

motion.name: Recommendations / Living ink
motion.trigger: Select another recommendation by timer, swipe, indicator or keyboard.
motion.motion: Letters lift from their original typeset positions, flutter and rearrange into the next quote. Matching characters travel within six font sizes; excess letters dissolve over475ms and new letters appear over812.5ms. All letter timings run25%longer with gentler cubic-bezier(.45,0,.25,1) easing. The original quote remains intact under an aria-hidden temporary layer. Letters animate opacity and transform; one temporary layer softly blurs0→0.65→0.35→0px over1250ms. In the final250ms (1000–1250ms), complementary ease-in-out opacity animations dissolve the copies into the exact original text run. Copies are fully transparent before cleanup, avoiding a glyph-shaping or rasterization snap. The original text at rest stays sharp. Responsive excerpts keep one visible paragraph; glyph measurements use that paragraph when desktop and mobile text differ. The author fades in over400ms after a375ms delay.
motion.playback: About and cases with multiple testimonials open on a random slide without changing the source order. No idle letter motion and no first-paint effect. The existing native 12-second progress clock stays independent; desktop hover keeps it and automatic selection running. Rapid selection cancels old copies; resize, font swap, offscreen/hidden/menu settle the selected quote. Tallest-slide grid reserves height. Author names and LinkedIn company links keep a permanent1px underline at24%ink opacity; the full two-line attribution and photo share the caption fade. letterMotion:false restores the prior350ms fade for a narrow rollback.
motion.reduced: No letter copies, movement or caption fade. The selected original quote is immediately readable; manual controls remain available.

motion.name: More About / Reading flow
motion.trigger: Scroll past the final project.
motion.timing: Native scroll distance · no timed transition
motion.motion: The last work and More About share a moving boundary without overlap, fading or recession of the work. Mobile releases the last work from sticky positioning and gives its final button96px of trailing space, equal to the96px before the photo gallery; its existing heading position is preserved. Desktop moves both edges together at scroll speed. The footer keeps its existing covering transition, with gradual fading and recession of More About.
motion.playback: Reverses directly with scrolling. Work media preparation, entrances, menu lock, anchors and footer corner treatment stay shared.
motion.reduced: Ordinary document flow, with the existing reduced-motion footer behavior.

motion.name: About teaser / Photo stream
motion.trigger: The prepared About photo scene is visible.
motion.motion: The same27 About photos, six-column arrangement, relative sizes and crops form a coherent periodic field. Desktop uses the original arrangement at half scale. Mobile preserves column order and sizes, keeps photos upright with the original compact seams and complete lower edges, with clipping only at the top. Wider periods avoid showing the same photo twice in one frame. The whole field moves slowly right and up on desktop, following the About gallery principle. Mobile moves horizontally to keep lower photo edges intact. No individual levitation.
motion.playback: CSS transforms pause offscreen below the scene, beneath an open menu or a fully covered scene, and in a hidden tab. Passed photos keep moving while their flow section remains exposed, preserving native browser translucency. Shared media mounts the repeated image pool once and prepares its actual elements before scene reveal, without delaying the homepage entrance.
motion.reduced: One static accessible composition; repeated pages are hidden.

anchors: animation:home-photo-stream 80s linear infinite paused,home-photo-rise 160s linear infinite paused

motion.name: Gallery / Ambient drift
motion.trigger: The photo field is visible and no manual interaction is active.
motion.timing: Right 8 px/s · up 4 px/s · resume after 500 ms
motion.motion: Twenty-seven photos repeat in six staggered columns with comparable portrait and landscape areas, preserved ratios and 21.84px design-space seams (86.4% coverage). Desktop photos smoothly grow toward the center: full-size center and 92% edge scale, with full-size slots reserved to prevent overlap. Mobile keeps 96% edge scale. The experiment keeps a 420px desktop / 308px mobile field. About uses 460px desktop / 338px mobile base height, plus the existing prose and footer allowances (600.8px / 466.8px total). Its background starts 20px farther below the preceding text, leaving 44.8px of overlap. The field drifts diagonally up-right; drag and arrow keys pan it directly. The experiment keeps internal top/bottom 15% fades and 36px desktop / 24px mobile prose gaps. About uses a 180px top white/blur fade, no bottom fade and 40px of photo content behind the rounded footer corners.
motion.playback: Hover keeps ambient motion running; keyboard focus stops it. Manual input defers it for 500 ms; wheel/trackpad scroll the page normally over photos. Offscreen, hidden tab and open menu stop rendering. No caption or horizontal fade.
motion.reduced: Ambient drift and release inertia are disabled; manual direct panning remains available. No pause/play control.

motion.name: Control / Surface feedback
motion.usage: AI brief · Back · shared pill frame
motion.trigger: Hover or press an enabled control.
motion.motion: Background and border colors transition within the fixed control frame; control dimensions stay stable. Disabled More Details and the Manual copy heading do not animate on activation.
motion.playback: Reverses to the default colors when hover/press ends. Manual copy keeps the existing heading and native logos mounted.
motion.reduced: Brief and Back feedback changes immediately; disabled states remain static.

motion.name: Link / Underline
motion.trigger: Hover a link; keyboard focus also reveals the header underline.
motion.motion: The 1 px line scales horizontally from 0 → 1 using cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). It follows the label width; the transform origin switches to make entry and exit directional.
motion.playback: Reverses on pointer leave. Mobile menu links have their own presentation; footer hover is limited to hover-capable fine pointers. Keyboard focus uses the shared outline.
motion.reduced: The underline changes immediately.

motion.name: AI brief / Logo motion
motion.usage: Light & Dark AI brief · Homepage · About
motion.trigger: Desktop fine-pointer hover, or activate the enabled Brief button.
motion.motion: Hover moves each logo 0 → −2 → 0 px, with a 140 ms step. Leaving hover returns current poses to baseline over 240 ms. Activation sends one −9 px wave with a 70 ms step, starting from current poses. Each half uses cubic-bezier(.37,0,.63,1).
motion.playback: Hover loops only while eligible. A click wave finishes before hover can resume; repeated clicks keep the current wave. Manual copy disables motion; hiding the tab cancels it.
motion.reduced: No logo movement. Mobile has no hover loop; normal activation can still play the single wave when reduced motion is off.

motion.name: AI brief / Copy confirmation
motion.usage: Light & Dark AI brief · Homepage · About
motion.trigger: The prompt is copied successfully.
motion.timing: 320 ms fade · next label starts at 360 ms
motion.motion: Fade the outgoing label out, leave a 40 ms separation, then fade in the other label over 320 ms using cubic-bezier(.4,0,.2,1). The check shares the Copied label’s opacity; the button frame stays fixed.
motion.playback: Copied is requested for 2200 ms after success, then the sequence reverses to Brief your AI. Copy failure exposes selectable Manual copy instead.
motion.reduced: Labels switch immediately; confirmation and manual-copy behavior remain available.

motion.name: Scroll / Work panels
motion.trigger: Actual page scrolling through the intro and project panels.
motion.motion: The next work panel covers the previous work. The final work scrolls out alongside More About without overlap; see More About / Reading flow. An ordinary outgoing project fades 1 → 0 and scales 1 → 0.975. The intro has its own recede: opacity 1 → .38, scale 1 → .955 and up to −18 px. Mobile enables each native sticky surface only during its actual cover interval and preserves normal reading space for taller cards.
motion.playback: Stopping scroll holds the pose; reversing scroll restores it. Fully covered surfaces become inert. Resize preserves the current reading position. The live homepage owns this composition; the card specimen documents its content.
motion.reduced: Ordinary readable list without overlapping transforms. Short/fallback layouts keep content in flow.

motion.name: Scroll / Contact footer
motion.trigger: The contact footer covers the preceding content.
motion.timing: Scroll progress · corners flatten in final quarter
motion.motion: The outgoing surface fades and recedes to scale 0.975. Footer upper corners go from 40px → 0 after 75% cover, using smoothstep. The incoming footer follows native sticky/scroll geometry.
motion.playback: Reverse scrolling restores the previous surface and round corners. On HOME and reading pages, the footer first scrolls in naturally until the complete Let’s talk heading is visible; only then does the preceding content pin, fade and recede. HOME uses the same measured heading depth in mobile sticky, desktop scene and native desktop layouts. Sticky positioning is enabled only during the actual reading/footer overlap; ordinary article scrolling remains in normal flow to preserve native Safari translucency. Menu scroll lock and hidden tabs preserve the current pose.
motion.reduced: Footer follows content in ordinary flow; the overlap effect is removed.

motion.name: Scroll / Native browser translucency
motion.usage: Homepage mobile panels · About desktop & mobile
motion.trigger: Normal reading, followed by the actual overlap interval.
motion.timing: Native scroll · sticky only while covering
motion.motion: Keep reading surfaces in normal document flow. Enable position: sticky only while the following surface covers them: data-scene-sticky on mobile HOME, reading-footer-overlap on reading pages. Keep measured heights and offsets stable so enabling sticky does not move the content. HOME retains touch scene and card viewport heights while the width stays unchanged, including in-app browsers that resize svh/lvh during toolbar motion; width/layout changes remeasure. The footer remains fluid to fill the current viewport.
motion.playback: Reverse scrolling restores the preceding surface and removes sticky outside the overlap. On reading pages, wait until the complete Let’s talk heading is visible before pinning. This avoids a large inactive sticky surface contributing a solid fill to Safari’s upper browser region. Safari owns the native blur/translucency; the site adds no glass overlay, edge filter or browser-specific branch. Appearance depends on the browser and its settings.
motion.reduced: All content remains in ordinary flow; overlapping sticky scenes are disabled. Menu scroll lock pauses scene updates, and resize remeasures the existing layout.

motion.name: Navigation / Work anchor
motion.usage: Homepage · header/footer Work links & scene navigation
motion.trigger: Activate navigation to a work section.
motion.motion: Animate the real scroll position to the requested scene; the same scene renderer paints the intermediate panel poses.
motion.playback: The destination receives focus once its content is visible when requested. User scrolling cancels the active navigation tween. Fallback layouts position the page immediately.
motion.reduced: Navigate immediately with readable focus targets.

motion.name: Status / Coming Soon
motion.trigger: The current project action is visible and uncovered.
motion.motion: The original 12px dot pulses opacity .4 → 1 → .4. Text and the disabled action stay still.
motion.playback: Pauses offscreen, when the document is hidden, behind the mobile menu or when its surface is covered. Continues while visible.
motion.reduced: Static dot at full opacity.

motion.name: Loading / Library SVGs
motion.trigger: A visible, slowly loaded native SVG or a complete Brief logo row finishes decoding.
motion.motion: Fade 0 → 1 using cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). Brief logos appear as one prepared row; ready/offscreen assets appear immediately.
motion.playback: The gallery prepares actual image nodes in visual order. State changes do not restart loading or replace the SVGs. This loading presentation belongs only to the DS.
motion.reduced: Prepared assets appear immediately without a fade.
